Sohna Road homes and their water

Sohna Road has a wide spread of housing: mid-rise and high-rise societies, builder floors, independent houses and a lot of mixed commercial buildings. Water arrangements vary just as much. Some homes are on piped supply, while others rely partly on tankers or a borewell, especially when supply runs short.

That mix matters for your tanks. Tanker and borewell water often carries more sand and sediment than treated supply, so where homes rely partly on it, silt and sediment tend to build up faster. Borewell water can also be hard, and over time it may leave a whitish scale on tank walls.

Signs your tank is due for a clean

  • Fine sand or brown particles at the bottom of a bucket
  • Your RO or tap pre-filter clogging sooner than it used to
  • A musty smell when the water first comes on
  • Green or black patches on the walls or under the lid of a rooftop tank
  • Low flow from taps even when the tank is full, often from sediment in the outlet
  • More than 6 months since the last clean, or you can't remember when it was

What we clean along Sohna Road

For houses and builder floors we clean rooftop plastic tanks and underground concrete sumps. The sump is where tanker water lands first, so it usually holds the thickest sludge, and cleaning it with the rooftop tank keeps the rooftop tank cleaner for longer. For societies and RWAs we offer bulk rates for 5 or more tanks and schedule cleaning tower by tower; see society tank cleaning.

Nobody goes inside any tank. A sludge pump pulls out the silt, a high-pressure jet washes the walls, floor and lid, and a food-safe disinfectant is followed by a clean-water flush and drying. The jet also lifts loose scale, though very old, hard crust may not come off completely. Each tank takes about 60 to 90 minutes, and you get before and after photos on WhatsApp.

Booking a clean

Questions

We use tanker water often. Should we clean more often than every 6 months?

Every 6 months is the usual rule. If you see sand in buckets or your filters clog well before that, an earlier clean, especially of the sump, makes sense.

Can you remove the white scale from borewell water?

The jet wash removes loose scale and deposits. Very old, hard crust may not come off fully, and we show you the result in the after photos.

Do you clean tanks in commercial or mixed-use buildings here?

Yes, if they are rooftop plastic tanks or underground concrete sumps. Send the number and size of tanks on WhatsApp for a quote.
